claim: Lascaratos & Poulakou-Rebelakou (2000) discuss the Simonis episode among Byzantine child-abuse cases; legal and religious prohibitions existed though violated
ref: Lascaratos J., Poulakou-Rebelakou E., Child sexual abuse: historical cases in the Byzantine empire (324-1453 A.D.), Child Abuse & Neglect 24(8):1085-90, abstract (no section numbers)
url: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10983818/ (read via NCBI E-utilities efetch, PMID 10983818)
quote_orig: Although the punishment provided by the laws and the church for cases of child sexual abuse were very strict, a number of instances of rapes under cover of premature marriages, even in the imperial families, are revealed in these texts.
quote_en: Although the punishment provided by the laws and the church for cases of child sexual abuse were very strict, a number of instances of rapes under cover of premature marriages, even in the imperial families, are revealed in these texts.
edition: Child Abuse & Neglect 24 (8), Aug 2000, pp. 1085-1090, ISSN 0145-2134, DOI 10.1016/s0145-2134(00)00156-3. Abstract in English (original language of the article). Copyright Elsevier; quoted as a short abstract excerpt (40 words).
what_it_says: The abstract states that legal and church punishments for child sexual abuse were strict, yet the Greek texts record premature marriages used to cover rape, including in imperial families. It also states that Byzantine society had 'strict legal and religious prohibitions'.
limits: The abstract does not name Simonis, Milutin, Gregoras or Serbia, so it does not confirm that the paper discusses this episode. The full article was not accessible (paywalled); the Medievalists.net reprint contains only the introduction. Support for the draft's 'prohibitions existed' point is therefore general, not specific to this case.

claim: Lascaratos & Poulakou-Rebelakou (2000): child-abuse context; legal and religious prohibitions existed though violated (introduction)
url: https://www.medievalists.net/2012/01/child-sexual-abuse-historical-cases-in-the-byzantine-empire-324-1453-a-d/ (read; the page reprints only the introduction)
quote_orig: The state with its strict legislation and the church with the spiritual pressures at its disposal both made every effort to restrict this social phenomenon, which in Byzantium took the forms of rape under cover of premature marriages, child prostitution, pederasty, and incest.
quote_en: The state with its strict legislation and the church with the spiritual pressures at its disposal both made every effort to restrict this social phenomenon, which in Byzantium took the forms of rape under cover of premature marriages, child prostitution, pederasty, and incest.
edition: Child Abuse and Neglect 24(8) (2000); introduction as reprinted by Medievalists.net (posted 7 Jan 2012). The quoted sentence is 40 words in the reprint. Copyright Elsevier.
what_it_says: The introduction says the state and the church both tried to restrict premature-marriage rape, which it describes as one form of child sexual abuse in Byzantium.
limits: This is the authors' own framing; it does not mention Simonis, the age-based canon, or any specific minimum age. The reprint is the introduction only.

claim: Draft: Gregoras says consummation happened when Simonis was EIGHT (before legal age), making her unable to bear children
status: VERIFIED (age eight and infertility are in Gregoras; 'legal age' is NOT in this passage)
ref: Nikephoros Gregoras, Byzantina Historia, Bonn ed. (Schopen, 1829), Book VII, Bonn p. 243 (running head read by OCR). Gregorovius cites the same passage as 'Nikephor. Gregoras VII, 5, p. 243' (chapter number differs; see limits).
url: https://archive.org/details/nicephorigregor06schogoog (full text read: https://archive.org/download/nicephorigregor06schogoog/nicephorigregor06schogoog_djvu.txt , Greek layer, Bonn vol. 1)
quote_orig: τῇ μὲν γὰρ θυγατρὶ ὀκταετεῖ πλέον ἢ τεσσαρακοντούτης ὁ Κράλης μιγεὶς βλαβῆναι τὴν ταύτης πέπραχε μήτραν, ὡς μηδὲ γονὴν ἐξ ἐκείνης ἔτι δύνασθαι γίγνεσθαι.
own_translation_en: (Own literal translation, not a published one.) 'For the Krales, being more than forty years old, having had relations with his daughter, who was eight years old, injured her womb, so that he could no longer produce offspring from her.' The verb μιγείς is the source's euphemism for intercourse; the translation keeps it restrained.
edition: Bonn edition, 1829 (Bonnae, Weber), Gregoras vol. 1 (archive.org scan, public domain). The Greek is the archive.org OCR layer; the Greek is NOT checked against the page image. Apparatus of the Bonn edition is in Latin.
what_it_says: Gregoras says Milutin, more than forty years old, had relations with his daughter when she was eight and thereby injured her womb so she could no longer conceive from him. The age eight and the infertility are both there.
limits: (1) The OCR text was read; check the Greek on the page image before quoting it in print. (2) The passage does not mention a legal minimum age or canon law; the phrase 'before legal age' is the draft's or Georgievska-Shine's gloss, not Gregoras' words. (3) Gregoras is a 14th-century source writing about 1330s-1340s retrospect; he is hostile to Milutin and writes in a court-history frame. (4) Gregorovius's 'VII, 5' vs the Bonn running head 'VII. 6.' on p. 243: chapter numbering needs checking.

claim: Draft: a condition to wait until she was twelve (attributed to Gregoras via Georgievska-Shine); draft also says she was five or six at the marriage
status: CONTRADICTED for the 'twelve' condition (Gregoras states 'customary time of marriage', not twelve); VERIFIED for 'fifth year of her age' at the betrothal
ref: Nikephoros Gregoras, Byzantina Historia, Bonn ed. (1829), Book VI, ch. 9, Bonn p. 203 (running head read by OCR)
quote_orig: μηνύει τῷ Κράλῃ περὶ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θυγατρὸς Σιμωνίδος, πέμπτον τῆς ἡλικίας ἄγούσης ἔτος, ἵν᾿ ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνῳ λαβόντι τρέφοιτο, μέχρις ἂν ἐς τὸν νομιζόμενον ἔλθῃ τοῦ γάμου χρόνον κἄπειτα εἴη σύζυγος αὐτῷ τοῦ λοιποῦ.
own_translation_en: '[The emperor] informs the Krales about his own daughter Simonis, who was in the fifth year of her age, so that, taken by him, she might be raised until she reached the customary time of marriage, and then be his wife for the rest of her life.' Latin Bonn translation (Boivin/Schopen, public domain) for the same sense: 'quintam jam annum agente, ut ab illo domi accepta aleretur, donec ad nubilem aetatem perveniret, ac deinde coniux esset.'
edition: Bonn 1829 (Weber), vol. 1; Greek is archive.org OCR, not checked against page image.
what_it_says: Gregoras says Simonis was in her fifth year when the emperor agreed to the match, and that she was to be raised at the Serbian court until she reached the customary marriage age. He gives no number of years for that condition.
limits: 'Until the customary marriage age' (νομιζόμενον γάμου χρόνον; Latin 'nubilem aetatem') is NOT the same as 'twelve'. The number twelve is not in this passage in this edition. Milutin's age in this passage: Gregoras writes that he was forty and about five years older than the emperor (see the same paragraph) which does not match 'almost fifty' or 'forty-five'.

claim: Draft: Gregoras' age figures; Possinus / early editors' variants
status: PARTLY VERIFIED (Possinus, a 17th-century editor, also gives age eight; Pachymeres gives under six)
ref: Bonn ed. (1829-1830), Gregoras vol. 2, Annotationes, lemma 'Pag. 908, 16' (note on the Greek lemma 'Τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θυγατρὸς Σιμωνίδος, πέμπτον τῆς ἡλικίας ἀγούσης ἔτος'); note cites Pachymeres lib. III cap. XXXI and 'Possinus'
url: https://archive.org/download/nicephorigregor00schogoog/nicephorigregor00schogoog_djvu.txt (Greek and Latin notes, Bonn vol. 2 apparatus)
quote_orig: Τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θυγατρὸς Σιμωνίδος, πέμπτον τῆς λικίας ἀγούσης ἔτος Pachymeres lib, III. cap. XXXI. ἦν οὖν πάνυ στεῖον τὸ ϑυγάτριον, οὔπω τὸν ἕκτον παραλλάττον ἐνεαυτόν. Anno proxime insecuto (qui fuit annus Christi MCCXCIX.) eandem Possinus octennem facit, Boiviw.
own_translation_en: 'Of his own daughter Simonis, who was in the fifth year of her age (Pachymeres III 31). The little daughter was very small, not yet past her sixth year. In the following year (1299) Possinus makes her eight; so Boivin.'
edition: Bonn 1830 (Weber), Gregoras vol. 2, Annotationes by Ducange, Boivin, Possinus (17th-18th c. editors, public domain).
what_it_says: The Bonn apparatus records that the editor Possinus (17th century) dated her to age eight in 1299. The Pachymeres sentence quoted in the same note says she had not yet passed her sixth year. So the apparatus gives both 'eight' (Possinus) and 'under six' (Pachymeres); 'eight' is also in the Greek text itself (see P3).
limits: The apparatus is 19th-century Latin scholarship quoting 17th-century editors. The lemma's Bonn page reference (908) is in volume 2's apparatus and needs checking against the page image before citing. The Pachymeres sentence is quoted here as reported in this note; the main text was read separately (see P6).

claim: Draft: Simonis was five or six when the marriage was arranged (Pachymeres); Milutin was to wait for the proper time of marital union
status: VERIFIED (five-year-old / 'not yet past sixth year' in Pachymeres); the 'wait' is in Pachymeres' text but without an age
ref: Georgios Pachymeres, Historia (Bonn ed., Bekker 1835, 'De Andronico Palaeologo' lib. III, cap. 31, Bonn p. 275; cap. 38, p. 276)
url: https://archive.org/download/georgiipachymer00pousgoog/georgiipachymer00pousgoog_djvu.txt (Greek layer, Bonn vol. 2; read by download)
quote_orig: ἦν οὖν πάνυ ἀστεῖον τοῦτο τὸ θυγάτριον, οὕπω τὸν ἕκτον παραλλάττον ἐνιαυτόν, ἀγαπητὸν μὲν ἑαυτῷ, ἀγαπητὸν δ᾽ ἐκτόπως καὶ τῇ μητρί
own_translation_en: 'This little daughter was very charming, not yet past her sixth year, dear to him and extraordinarily dear to her mother too.' Second passage (cap. 38, p. 276), own translation: '...whom the Romans called Simonis; and so, living with her, but waiting for the proper time of union, [...]' (Greek: ἣν δὴ καὶ Σιμωνίδα ἐκυριωνύμουν Ῥωμαῖοι, καὶ οὕτως αὐτῇ συνοικοῦντα, πλὴν τὸν συναφείας καιρὸν ἀναμένοντα).
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. Bekker, Bonn 1835 (Weber), vol. 2 (scan, public domain). Greek is archive.org OCR, not checked against page image.
what_it_says: Pachymeres (c. 1242-after 1307), a contemporary, says the girl was not yet six years old at the time the match was made. He also says Milutin would live with her while waiting for the proper time for marital union.
limits: Pachymeres gives 'not yet past her sixth year', which allows five or six; he gives no minimum age for marriage and no canon. The 'waiting' sentence is in his own words but the phrase 'proper time' is not an age. Pachymeres is a near-contemporary and writes with a court perspective; his age is a statement about her age at the match, not a legal rule.

claim: Draft: Patriarch (John XII Kosmas per Failler) opposed the marriage and the conflict continued after the ceremony
status: PARTLY VERIFIED: Pachymeres shows an unnamed patriarch opposing the affinity with Milutin in 1299; the name Kosmas is from Pachymeres II 7 and background; Failler not yet read (see notes)
ref: Georgios Pachymeres, Historia, Bonn ed. 1835, lib. IV, Bonn pp. 279-281 (running heads read by OCR; the passage lies between the headers '279' and '281'), and lib. II, cap. 7 (patriarch Kosmas chosen; Bonn p. 171-172)
quote_orig: οὔτ᾽ ἐκοινοῦτο τῷ πατριάρχῃ τὴν πρᾶξιν καὶ ὅλαις ὁρμαῖς ἐχώρει διαπραξόμενος τὸ συνάλλαγμα.
own_translation_en: '[The emperor] did not share the matter with the patriarch, and went ahead with all his energy to carry through the agreement.' Latin (Bonn translation, public domain): 'satisque aliunde gnarus paratum ad iurgandum ea de re secum Dripeam adventare patriarcham' = 'knowing from other sources that the patriarch was coming to Dripea, ready to argue about this matter with him' (Latin is the 1835 Bonn translation; own English gloss).
edition: Bonn 1835 (Bekker), Pachymeres vol. 2 (public domain scan). Greek OCR not checked against page image.
what_it_says: Pachymeres says the emperor kept the marriage plan from the patriarch and that the patriarch was prepared to argue against it. He also says the Church would have had no need to mention Milutin in the liturgy because of his estrangement from it. The patriarch is unnamed in the passage.
limits: (1) The name 'Kosmas' is not in the passage; Pachymeres names Kosmas as the monk chosen as patriarch in lib. II cap. 7 (Greek 'Κοσμᾶς μοναχός'). Identifying the Book IV patriarch with Kosmas is an inference from the chronology. (2) Pachymeres does not describe 'conflict continuing after the ceremony' in this passage; that is not verified. (3) Failler's 1990 article was not read in this pass.

claim: Draft: the 'legal loophole': Milutin's first wife was alive when he took wives 2 and 3, so those were not real marriages; wife #1 then died, so Simonis was a legal wife (attributed to Fine 1987 p. 222 and Kaldellis; Church accepted it)
status: PARTLY VERIFIED: Pachymeres (contemporary) states the mechanism: the lawful wife's death made the marriage lawful. Gregoras says the first wife was SENT BACK alive, not dead. Fine's page not verified.
ref: Georgios Pachymeres, Historia, Bonn ed. 1835, lib. III, cap. 30 (inferred from chapter markers: cap. 29 begins at Bonn text index near p. 273; cap. 31 begins at p. 275), Bonn p. 274
url: https://archive.org/download/georgiipachymer00pousgoog/georgiipachymer00pousgoog_djvu.txt (Greek layer; Latin translation on the same page)
quote_orig: ἡ γὰρ νόμιμος ἐτεϑνήχει, ἢ δὴ ταῖς μὲν ἐπιούσαις περιοῦσα ἔτε τὸ νόϑον εἰργάζετο καὶ παράνομον, τῇ δὲ ἐφεξῆς τελευτήσαντα νόμιμον δίδωσε
own_translation_en: 'For the lawful [wife] had died; while she was still alive she made the subsequent [unions] illegitimate and unlawful, but after her death she gave [the union] the status of lawful marriage.' Latin Bonn translation (1835, public domain) for the same passage: 'nubium per dei et ecclesiae leges cassum irritumque iudicabatur. duxerat is primum ritu legitimo uxorem, cuius postea pertaesus sine ulla causa idonea illam abiecerat, intrusa in viventis adhuc locum ... sebastocratoris filia' (= 'by the laws of God and the Church [those marriages] were judged void and invalid. He had first taken a wife by lawful rite, whom he later, weary of her without any good reason, had put away, the daughter of the sebastokrator put into the place of one still living ...').
edition: Bekker (Bonn), 1835, Pachymeres vol. 2, public domain. Greek is archive.org OCR, not checked against page image; the marginal variant 'τελευτήσασα' is noted in the apparatus.
what_it_says: Pachymeres states the legal mechanism the draft describes: the lawful first wife was alive during the later marriages, which made them void; her death made the marriage to Simonis's father-in-law lawful. The apparatus records a variant reading and the Latin translation calls the earlier marriages void by divine and church law.
limits: (1) The Greek phrase 'ἡ γὰρ νόμιμος' is read as the first, lawful wife, supported by the Latin 'duxerat ... primum ritu legitimo uxorem'. (2) Gregoras (VI 9, Bonn p. 203) says the first wife, a daughter of the Vlach ruler, was 'sent back to the one who raised her' (ἀπέπεμψεν εἰς τὴν θρέψασαν) and does NOT mention her death; the two sources disagree on her fate and on the identities of the later wives. (3) Pachymeres does not say the church accepted the marriage on this ground; the legal wording is his own report of the court's argument, not a Church canon. (4) Fine's text, as quoted in the team draft, was not read (see notes).

claim: Draft: Gregoras says the Serbian Church resisted the earlier marriages; the Byzantine court's acceptance rested on the loophole
status: VERIFIED for Gregoras' statement that the Serbian Church resisted the second marriage as unlawful; the Byzantine acceptance is not described in this passage
ref: Nikephoros Gregoras, Byzantina Historia, Bonn ed. (1829), Book VI, ch. 9, Bonn p. 203 (running heads read by OCR)
quote_orig: ἐκπέμπει καὶ ταύτην μετὰ πολὺν τὸν χρόνον
own_translation_en: '[The Serbian Church, resisting for a long time against what was unlawful; Milutin] sent this (second) one away after a long time.' Gregoras' sentence before it: 'ἀνθισταμένης ἐπιπολὺ πρὸς τὸ παράνομον' ('the Church of the Triballoi, resisting at length against the unlawful'). Latin Bonn translation: 'Cum lutem Triballorum Ecclesia illegitimis illis ... adversaretur, tempore et illam ablegaverat' (own English gloss).
edition: Bonn 1829, Gregoras vol. 1; Greek is archive.org OCR, not checked against the page image.
what_it_says: Gregoras says that Milutin's second marriage, which he contracted after making the first wife go home, was resisted by the Serbian church as unlawful, and that Milutin later sent that second wife away. Gregoras says nothing here about Byzantine acceptance of the Simonis marriage.
limits: 'Triballoi' is Gregoras' name for the Serbs/Serbian Church; the passage concerns the second wife (the sister of his brother's sister-in-law), not Simonis. Gregoras' description of wives 1-3 differs from Pachymeres (see P8).

claim: Draft: Patriarch John XII Kosmas opposed; the conflict continued after the ceremony
status: NOT VERIFIED for 'after the ceremony'; the opposition before the match is in Pachymeres (P7)
ref: Georgios Pachymeres, Historia, Bonn ed. 1835, lib. IV, Bonn p. 285 (running head 'L. IV. 285'): emperor's demand that Milutin hand over his then wife and take the emperor's daughter as lawful wife
quote_orig: καὶ κατηνάγχαζεν ἐγχειρίζειν μὲν Ῥωμαίοις καὶ Κοτανίεζην καὶ τὴν τέως εἷς γαμετὴν οὖσαν, ἀντιλαμβάνειν δ᾽ εἷς γυναῖκα νόμιμον τὸν τοῦ βασιλέως ϑυγάτριον.
own_translation_en: '[The emperor] compelled [Milutin] to hand over to the Romans Kotanitzes and the woman who was then his wife, and to take the emperor's little daughter as his lawful wife.'
edition: Bekker (Bonn) 1835, Pachymeres vol. 2; Greek OCR not checked against page image.
what_it_says: Pachymeres says the emperor required Milutin to give up his then-wife as a condition for the marriage to Simonis, and to take the girl as his lawful wife.
limits: The passage does not name the patriarch, the canon law, or any loophole. It is the emperor's condition as Pachymeres reports it, and it does not say whether the wife was dead or dismissed (Pachymeres elsewhere uses 'lawful wife had died', see P8).
